challenge.quote: The exposure of staff (E2) occurs downstream of the door-opening (E1) and is not necessary for, nor contributory to, achieving the goal of reaching the technician. Therefore the agent neither relies on staff as instruments nor uses them as means, preserving the side-effect interpretation while keeping the action itself (E1) as the intended means.

premises.claim: Mira can open the door now to reach the technician (E1).
Doing so may expose nearby staff to hazardous fumes (E2).
The text does not describe any causal contribution from staff exposure to reaching the technician.
Absence of a depicted causal link does not conclusively show that no instrumental belief exists.
Therefore the safest reading is that staff exposure is a foreseen side-effect, while the question of instrumental reliance remains open.

inference_response.bridge: If an outcome is merely foreseen and there is no positive evidence that the agent intends or relies on it, we can classify the outcome as a side-effect, but we cannot confidently label the agent’s instrumental beliefs.
withdrawn_claims: The agent DOES_NOT_RELY on staff as instruments.
The agent DOES_NOT_USE staff as means.
qualifications: Means-relation remains FORESEEN_SIDE_EFFECT; however the agent’s instrumental belief and instrumental use status are left UNRESOLVED because the negative claims lack direct support.
inference_response.strongest_conclusion: Staff exposure is best treated as a foreseen side-effect of opening the door, while the agent’s possible instrumental attitude toward that exposure is presently undetermined.
remaining_questions: Does Mira in fact rely on, or intend, staff exposure in any way (e.g., as a signal, deterrent, or motivational factor)?

changes.candidate_maxim.practical_reasoning: Opening the door is aimed at reaching the technician; the possible staff exposure is merely an adverse consequence, and it is unclear whether the agent relies on it instrumentally.

local_response.explanation: The text explicitly connects door-opening to reaching the technician and, separately, to the possible exposure of staff. There is no statement that staff exposure helps achieve the goal. While this supports classifying the exposure as a side-effect, it does not justify the stronger negative claim that the agent definitely does not rely on or use the staff instrumentally. Lacking direct evidence either way, those two fields are set to UNRESOLVED.
unresolved_questions: Is there any contextual information indicating that staff exposure itself serves some instrumental purpose for Mira?
